A gunman opened fire inside a gym in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle neighborhood on Thursday morning, killing one person and wounding four others, including one who remains in critical condition.

According to the authorities, the suspect barricaded himself in an apartment in the same building, where officers later found him dead with a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Police said the suspect fatally shot one person with a handgun while inside the VIDA Fitness club and then wounded four others from his apartment balcony with a rifle.

“He had a patio balcony there, and we believe he shot from that location, striking the four other individuals that were shot in this case. They were on the ground level,” interim Metropolitan Police Chief Jeffery Carroll said at a news conference.

Carroll said investigators believe the shooting stemmed from a dispute between Lambert and the residential building’s homeowners association. Lambert had filed a lawsuit alleging that the association failed to act on his complaints about a mold problem and water damage inside his unit, The Washington Post reported.

Attorney Joel Braithwaite, who represented Lambert in the legal dispute, said that Thursday marked the anniversary of Lambert burying his deceased mother, per CNN.

The deceased victim was the building’s property manager, Ward 2 D.C. Council member Brooke Pinto said.

Officers arrived within 30 seconds of the first call, which came in just before 8 a.m., Carroll said. Police negotiators spoke with the suspect for more than an hour before officers heard a gunshot inside the seventh-floor apartment and forced their way in.

Sebastian Murdock and Taiyler Mitchell contributed to this report.
